title: Prompt Sundial — heuristic sketchbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick brain-dump / working notebook for a small prompt-library idea I keep circling back to: make prompt selection adaptive to "time-of-use" and micro-context signals (a.k.a. the "sundial" heuristic). Not polished — notes to self + few-shot drafts + failure cases to watch for.

Core hypothesis:
- Users' phrasing, patience, and desired verbosity shift with time and context (morning vs late-night vs in-product microflow). If we rotate a small set of templates tied to lightweight temporal/context signals we can reduce hallucinations and control verbosity/cost without heavy RL or policy infra.

Signals considered (cheap to compute):
- local_time_bucket: morning|afternoon|evening|late-night
- session_length (short|long) inferred from recent tokens
- user_mode (explore|task) — heuristic from route metadata
- latency_budget (low|normal) from front-end SLOs

Sundial strategy (sketch):
- Maintain 3 templates per intent: concise, balanced, explanatory.
- Map time_bucket x session_length -> preferred template.
- If latency_budget==low -> force concise.
- If user_mode==explore AND time_bucket==late-night -> prefer higher creativity template but add guard rails.

Prompt templates (examples) — intent: "summarize long article"
- concise: "TL;DR in 1–2 sentences, strictly factual. No added context. Use neutral tone."
- balanced: "Write a 3-sentence summary capturing main claim, 1 key supporting point, and one caveat."
- explanatory: "Summarize the article for a non-expert: main claim, 2 supporting points, why it matters, and one unanswered question."

Few-shot exemplars (for balanced):
- EX1: article about vaccine rollout -> "Main claim: X. Support: Y. Caveat: Z."
- EX2: op-ed about remote work -> "Main claim: A. Support: B. Caveat: C."
(keep terse; prefer structured outputs so downstream parsers can pick fields)

Guard rails / failure cases to watch:
- Temporal bias: test that 'late-night' template doesn't systematically inject uncertainty phrasing when article is factual — avoid 'sounds like' language unless evidence is weak.
- Mode misclassification: if session_length heuristic flips rapidly, ensure not oscillating templates mid-conversation. Add hysteresis.
- Overfitting exemplars: too-specific few-shots can bias to those domains — keep general phrasing.
- Cost regressions: ensure 'explanatory' path is used sparingly. Add per-user budget cap.

Quick experiment matrix (low-effort):
- A/B: baseline fixed balanced template vs sundial selection with same balanced exemplar set. Metrics: user satisfaction (thumbs), average tokens, hallucination rate (manual eval on 200 samples).
- Latency stress: activate concise forced when latency_budget low; measure error rate and perceived usefulness (micro-survey).
- Drift test: deploy for 2 weeks and measure template flip frequency per session (target <2 flips).

Debugging checklist (notes to self):
- Log chosen template + signals for every request (privacy-safe hash).
- Create small reference eval set (50 docs) across domains to check consistency across time buckets.
- Add 'forced template override' endpoint for SEs to repro.

Example prompt payload (internal testing only):
"""
SYSTEM: You are a summarization assistant. Return a JSON object with fields: "summary" (string), "support" (string), "confidence_level" (low|medium|high). Do NOT invent facts.
USER: [template injected here]
ARTICLE: <long text>
"""

Notes / open questions:
- How many time buckets are useful in practice? Start with 3 (morning/afternoon/night).
- Could replace time_bucket with 'circadian proxy' from user locale/timezone + usage patterns (privacy concerns).
- Might be worth pairing with short prompt-level evals to auto-tag templates that regress.

Next steps:
- Implement small simulator script to sample templates by synthetic signal distribution (Evan to pair?) -> run token-cost sims.
- Prototype logging + override endpoint -> Lina to spin up tiny lambda.
- Build 200-sample eval (domain split) and schedule manual pass.

Random scribbles:
- idea: 'sunrise' template = optimistic concise, 'dusk' = cautious explanatory
- hysteresis: don't change template unless signal stable for 2 requests OR 15s
- consider 'micro-messages' (single-sentence inline answers) as separate intent class

End of dump. Mostly want to get this into Drive before it mutates further. Revisit after first AB-run.
